messages:
maria: Quick report from onboarding loki-mini-int8: overall perf +2.8% latency but found two locale-specific failures on our smoke suites: (A) zh-vertical: ruby/furigana-like markers (private markers U+FFF9FFFB) are dropped intermittently; (B) ar-translation: bracket tokens appear swapped in output for some short parenthesis cases.

jun: can you share the exact eval flags you used? quant cfg? sampling?

maria: Eval command: `./runtests --model loki-mini --quant int8 --suites zh_vertical,ar_sample --decode topk=40,temporal=0.8 --seed 7`. qconf used `int8_packed_v1`. Runtime: KV cache enabled, dynamic batching on.

oliver: any diffs vs fp16 baseline token streams? need raw token ids + codepoints.

maria: pasted sample below, baseline vs int8 output for en->ar example:
```
# en source: "Please check (x, y)."
# baseline token codepoints: [0x0627,0x0644,0x0641,0x0638,0x0644,0x0627,0x0020,0x0028,0x0078,0x002C,0x0020,0x0079,0x0029,0x002E]
# loki-mini-int8 token codepoints: [0x0627,0x0644,0x0641,0x0638,0x0644,0x0627,0x0020,0x0029,0x0078,0x002C,0x0020,0x0079,0x0028,0x002E]
```
so parentheses codepoints flipped positions (8th and 13th) not just rendering.

jun: interesting. that implies generation order changed. does disabling kv-cache fix it?

maria: yes: `--runtime no-kvcache` gives same tokens as baseline. With kv-cache on it's deterministic in failure.

jun: good repro. I suspect a cache write/read offset bug in the packed-kernel path when sequence length crosses a certain multiple. Can you try `--batch-size 1 --max-seq 64` and also run with `--kernel scalar` to force different kernel set?

maria: ran `--batch-size 1 --kernel scalar` still fails with kv-cache on. But `--runtime no-kvcache` passes. Ran `--max-seq 32` and it passes; fails at 64 consistently.

oliver: that pinpoints an indexing overflow/stride issue when seq_len >= 64 in kv cache vectorized path. I'll start a bisect on the kernel selection commits touching kv_pack offsets.

maria: on the zh side, here's a sample where private ruby markers are missing:
```
# src snippet vertical: "漢字[\uFFF9ruby\uFFFB]"
# baseline tokens contain 0xFFF9 sequence; loki-mini-int8 output omits 0xFFF9..0xFFFB region and collapses to bare kanji.
```
Hit-rate stats: baseline keep-rate 98.7% for marker tokens; loki-mini-int8 61.4% keep-rate on zh_vertical suite.

jun: that sounds like quant noise pushing low-prob control markers under sampling threshold. Do we have topk probability mass for those markers? try `--verbose-log-probs` for a couple of samples.

maria: pasted one logits snippet (truncated)
```
# step 14 logits (selected indices): marker U+FFF9 idx=5234 logit -2.1 -> prob 0.11
# in int8 run: idx=5234 logit -5.6 -> prob 0.0038
```
so the logit dropped a lot.

jun: run a calibration pass with `--force-quant-calib --calib-samples 5000` and also try a mixed-precision fallback for special Unicode ranges via `--precision-exempt 0xFFF0-0xFFFF` so marker logits computed in fp16. If that restores hit-rate, it's a quant rounding failure.

oliver: for the kv-cache bug I'll instrument the pack/unpack offsets and run a microbench loop reproducer. If it's stride math, a minimal C test should reproduce without the model. I'll open ML-3799 and assign to infra-kernels.

devops-bot: issue created: ML-3799 "kv-cache stride/offset bug reproducing bracket reorder in int8 pack path" assigned to @oliver, due 2025-01-15.

eval-bot: eval run created: EVAL-8921 linking to test vectors, zh_vertical/ar_sample; logs uploaded at s3://redwood-evals/loki-mini/int8/1755568888/

maria: next steps: (1) jun to test force-calib + precision-exempt and report hit-rate delta; (2) oliver to bisect kernel commits & provide microbench; (3) I'll gather affected sample ids and mark P0 for ar bracket corruption since customer-facing. Triage 10am PT tomorrow.

jun: will try precision-exempt today and post numbers.

maria: thanks all. keeping notes in ML-3799 and EVAL-8921. I'll attach short repro tarball there.

oliver: if anyone else hits similar locale-only reorder drop please @channel and paste one token-stream diff. small diffs help the kernel author triage quickly.

maria: filing links now, ping when ready.
